newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-ROCKETS EVEN SERIES WITH JAZZ ON JOHNSON BUZZER BEAT.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-ROCKETS EVEN SERIES WITH JAZZ ON JOHNSON BUZZER BEAT.

text.p: Eddie Johnson came off the bench to save the Houston Rockets for a second straight game Sunday, hitting a 3-pointer at the buzzer in a 95-92 victory over the Utah Jazz that evened the Western Conference finals at two games apiece.
"I'm 38 years old," said Johnson, who was mobbed by his teammates and near tears after hitting the game-winner. "Just to experience this -- not many 38-year-olds get to experience this."

Utah had four shots to take the lead on its final possession but Houston finally grabbed the rebound with 6.7 seconds remaining. After a timeout, the Rockets inbounded to Clyde Drexler, who was double-teamed and forced to pass.
Johnson got the ball five feet behind the 3-point arc with under a second left. He launched a shot that swished through as the buzzer sounded.
"In that situation, it's a no-pressure shot," said Johnson, who scored 31 points in a Game 3 win. "If I miss, we go to overtime."
However, he admitted, "I have never hit a bigger shot in my career."

"I hope that we know who Eddie Johnson is now," Jazz coach Jerry Sloan said. "We went and doubled the ball and left a great shooter wide open. It's very simple, we have five guys to cover their five guys and we didn't do that."
Rockets coach Rudy Tomjanovich admitted that the final play was called for centre Hakeem Olajuwon, but broke down.
"Johnson wasn't supposed to get the ball," Tomjanovich said. "But fortunately, he was in the right place at the right time."

"We were expecting them to go into Olajuwon," Utah guard Jeff Hornacek said. "I was there to put the trap on (point guard Matt) Maloney. He did a good job of rotating the ball to Eddie. If we have our choice of Olajuwon hitting his little jump hook or Eddie taking that shot from behind the 3-point line, we'll take that three anytime."

Johnson scored seven points. Olajuwon had 27 points and Charles Barkley came up big with 20 points and 16 rebounds for the Rockets, who have erased a 2-0 series deficit. En route to NBA titles in 1994 and 1995, Houston also overcame 2-0 deficits in the conference semifinals.
Game 5 is Thursday at Utah, where the Jazz are 7-0 in the postseason. They have never been to the NBA Finals.
"The pressure is on them now," said Olajuwon.
"We still have to play this team again and our guys have always bounced back after a tough game," Sloan said.
Barkley had criticised his teammates who had already won two championships for not playing with enough intensity. But he said that they showed plenty of fire this time.
"We're two games away from being done or we're two games away from the Finals," said Barkley. "They say it's not life and death and I say they're right, it's a lot more important than that."
Karl Malone had 22 points and 10 rebounds and John Stockton also had 22 points for the Jazz, who scored just 16 points in the fourth quarter.

"In a tough game like this, when you have an opportunity to win, you can't get too down on yourself," said Malone, who shot 10-of-28 from the field. "I like the intensity. I liked the way we played. But I'll be the first to admit I didn't have a great game."

"I just tried to cut down on his easy baskets and not foul him when he was shooting," said Barkley, who guarded Malone for much of the game. "But he's going to get his points. We did a really good job covering the other guys."
Drexler scored 16 points and Mario Elie added 11 for the Rockets, who shot 46 percent (33-of-72) from the field and held a 43-40 rebounding edge. Houston made 6-of-19 3-pointers.
Jeff Hornacek scored 14 points for the Jazz, who shot 42 percent (35-of-83) and committed just nine turnovers. However, Utah made just 2-of-8 3-pointers.
Both teams' leading scorers, Olajuwon and Malone, spent more time on the bench than they would have liked due to early foul trouble. REUTER
